Use explicit, goal-rich signals instead of only clicks and purchases: user comments and reviews can reveal the reasons behind decisions, helping align preferences, improve diversity, and make recommendations more explainable [1]. A related line of work models motivation or high-level intent so the system can understand not just what users choose, but why, and can ground reasoning in extracted intents rather than surface interaction patterns [2, 4].

Other papers extend this idea with richer user profiling and natural-language profiles that are editable and steerable, so users can directly express preferences that are hard to infer from behavior [3, 9]. More broadly, the surveys argue for LLM-based systems that make user representations more transparent, revisable, and aligned with user goals [5, 6].
